Part 1: Introduction to IBM Think 2023 and AI in Business
[The introduction to IBM Think 2023 conference highlights the fun and excitement of AI-generated art and music while emphasizing the importance of a higher standard for AI in business. The speaker explains that AI in business must be built to be trusted, secured, and adaptable, working across the organization and scaling across systems. AI in business should be able to show its work and not rely on a single system.]

Part 2: The Significance of AI and its Impact on Various Industries
[The speaker expresses their fascination with AI and its potential to impact every industry, from customer care to medicine, manufacturing, and energy. They acknowledge that while the pace of AI technology can be daunting and scary, the opportunities to harness foundation models and generative AI with proper governance are immense. The speaker encourages the audience to not just be AI users, but to become AI value creators by taking control of their data and models.]

Part 3: Becoming an AI Value Creator with Watson X
[The speaker introduces Watson X, IBM's integrated data and AI platform, which consists of three primary parts: watsonx.data, watsonx.ai, and watsonx.governance. The speaker explains that these components work together seamlessly throughout the entire lifecycle of foundation models and provide enterprises with the ability to train, validate, tune, and deploy traditional machine learning and foundation models. The platform is built on top of Red Hat OpenShift, allowing for seamless integration and deployment in any IT environment.]

Part 4: The AI Workflow in Watson X
[The speaker describes the end-to-end AI workflow in Watson X, which consists of data preparation, training the model, validating the model, tuning it, and deploying it in applications and solutions. They explain how watsonx.data establishes connections between data sources, allowing data scientists to access data easily and how WatsonX.data collects and categorizes data from various domains and languages. The speaker also discusses the process of filtering and preprocessing data, including removing duplicates, hate speech, and private information, and generating data cards to track different versions and subsets of data.]

Part 5: Training and Validating Models with Watson X.AI
[The speaker explains how Watson X.AI allows users to pick a model architecture from five families of IBM models and train it using computing resources across the hybrid cloud. They describe the process of tokenizing data according to the requirements of the model and how Watson X.AI simplifies the user experience by taking advantage of the best open source technology. The speaker also discusses the process of validating models by running extensive benchmarks and creating model cards that list all the details of the model.]

Part 6: Tuning Models with WatsonX.Governance
[The speaker explains how WatsonX.Governance combines the data card and model card to form a fact sheet, which is cataloged in .Governance. They also discuss the process of tuning models to adapt them to new downstream tasks, which is the basis for the large productivity gains afforded by foundation models. The speaker encourages users to leverage WatsonX.ai to access a rich set of open models and tune them using business proprietary data for specific tasks.]

Part 7: Deploying and Monitoring Models with Watson X
[The speaker explains how Watson X allows users to deploy models efficiently wherever they are needed, whether in the public cloud, on-premises, or on the edge. They also discuss the inference stack, which consists of state-of-the-art technology for scalable model serving. The speaker emphasizes the importance of continuously monitoring and updating models in both .data and .ai and describes the process of the data and model factory, which is central to solid and proper governance of AI.]

Part 8: The Importance of Community in AI
[The speaker emphasizes the importance of community in AI and the need to bet on the diversity and creativity of the open AI community. They announce a new partnership with Hugging Face, which will bring the power of the open source community to Watson X. The speaker also discusses the benefits of open source AI, including the ability to build smaller, more specialized, and customized models for specific use cases.]
